verified_claims.claim: Kartr presents itself as an end-to-end influencer-sponsor platform covering YouTube analysis, sponsor detection, relationship mapping, campaign execution, content generation and analytics.
Kartr has a public MIT-licensed repository with a React/Bun frontend, FastAPI backend, Firebase persistence, Gemini/Grok/Groq integrations, Tavily search and NetworkX graph code.
The normal public channel-analysis path fetches recent YouTube videos, performs deterministic sponsor matching and then sends a batch of descriptions to an LLM for structured sponsor extraction.
Kartr's public graph implementation maps creator_name to sponsor_name and exposes degree centrality, connected components and neighbor lists.
Both Devpost-linked Cloud Run deployments returned HTTP 500 during verification on 2026-08-24.

repository.assessment: Public hackathon prototype source is available, but its claimed live deployment was not functioning during verification and the repository does not include a reproducible creator-sponsor corpus.

actual_pipeline.name: collect_video_or_channel_metadata
actual_pipeline.implementation: Single-video analysis uses YouTube videos.list. Channel analysis uses search.list ordered by date, then a batch videos.list request, capped at 50 recent videos.

actual_pipeline.name: deterministic_sponsor_prepass
actual_pipeline.implementation: Lower-cased title and description are checked against a hard-coded common-sponsor dictionary, disclosure phrases and basic URL or promo-code regexes. A positive disclosure without a resolved brand falls back to the literal label Sponsored.

actual_pipeline.name: llm_enrichment
actual_pipeline.implementation: The batch prompt asks for index, is_sponsored, sponsor_name, discount_code, sponsor_url and high/medium/low confidence. Gemini is attempted first and Grok is the fallback. Results enrich or override the per-video fields.

actual_pipeline.name: manual_persistence
actual_pipeline.implementation: A separate save-analysis route persists the request to Firebase or CSV. The request accepts an untyped sponsors list and promotes only the first sponsor to top-level sponsor_name and sponsor_industry.

actual_pipeline.name: graph_and_rag
actual_pipeline.implementation: Top-level creator_name and sponsor_name fields become a simple creator-brand graph. NetworkX generates degree centrality and component counts, while a separate keyword-substring RAG path retrieves up to ten stored rows.

sponsor_extraction.single_video_context: Title, channel, up to 20 tags and at most 4,000 description characters.
sponsor_extraction.channel_context: The collector stores only the first 200 description characters; the later 800-character LLM slice therefore receives at most 200 characters on this path.
sponsor_extraction.multimodal_exception: A separate local MP4 upload path sends the video file to Gemini, but this is not the normal YouTube channel pipeline.
sponsor_extraction.confidence_semantics: High, medium or low is produced by the LLM prompt. No calibrated probability, labelled evaluation or post-generation substring/evidence gate is applied in the audited code.

information_loss: Repeated creator-brand observations collapse into one simple edge.
Direction, count, date, recency, confidence and evidence are not part of the graph edge.
Only the first saved sponsor is promoted to the field consumed by the graph.
Raw display names are node identifiers, so aliases can fragment one brand into multiple nodes.

recommendation_method.web_discovery: Tavily receives a broad niche query and returns at most five search results.
recommendation_method.formatting: An LLM is instructed to emit three recommendations with a fit_score constrained to 60-99.
recommendation_method.creator_matching: Keyword/name/channel matching and subscriber bonuses create a base score. An LLM rescores up to ten candidates; final score is 40% heuristic and 60% LLM.
recommendation_method.budget_filter_status: budget_min and budget_max parameters exist but are explicitly documented as future filtering and are not applied in the audited method.
recommendation_method.assessment: This is recommendation generation, not a calibrated evidence-backed ranking or a sponsor-gap algorithm.

testing_and_evidence.dedicated_sponsor_test_reviewed: One live MrBeast video smoke script that prints fields and returns a boolean.
testing_and_evidence.assessment: The public code demonstrates flow integration, not measured extraction accuracy.

gaps.subject: Kartr
gaps.fact: Devpost says Gemini analyzes transcripts, metadata and descriptions, and discusses spoken mentions and overlays.
gaps.observed_gap: No transcript or caption ingestion file was found in the complete public repository tree. The normal YouTube channel route processes metadata and descriptions; only a separate uploaded-MP4 route is multimodal.
gaps.impact_inference: The public implementation cannot substantiate the transcript and overlay coverage claimed for normal YouTube analysis.

gaps.subject: Kartr
gaps.fact: Devpost brands the system as Gemini 3-powered.
gaps.observed_gap: The audited public configuration defaults text analysis to gemini-2.0-flash, and the local uploaded-video function directly names gemini-1.5-flash. An environment variable could override the text default, but no deployed configuration is public.
gaps.impact_inference: Model-version marketing should not be treated as verified deployment configuration.

gaps.subject: Kartr
gaps.fact: Channel collection truncates returned descriptions to 200 characters before LLM sponsor enrichment.
gaps.observed_gap: The later 800-character slice cannot recover text discarded by the collector.
gaps.impact_inference: Disclosures, affiliate links and sponsor blocks placed later in a YouTube description can be missed.

gaps.subject: Kartr
gaps.fact: The LLM assigns sponsor name and qualitative confidence, and the audited merge accepts those fields without checking the proposed brand against the source text or a canonical registry.
gaps.observed_gap: There is no enforced evidence gate, alias normalization, blocklist or creator-owned-domain detection in the audited sponsor path.
gaps.impact_inference: Common citations, creator shops, ambiguous promo codes and model hallucinations can become graph nodes.

gaps.subject: Kartr
gaps.fact: The graph is a simple unweighted creator-name to first-sponsor-name projection.
gaps.observed_gap: It does not represent repeated buys, recency, campaign clusters, proof, contactability, X relationship degree or operator paths.
gaps.impact_inference: Degree centrality alone cannot support Solomon-rooted BD routing or distinguish a durable paid relationship from one noisy mention.

gaps.subject: MangoBD current sponsor-cluster module
gaps.fact: The current pilot contains 13 curated sponsorship observations, producing 12 creator-brand pairs and 10 campaign clusters.
gaps.observed_gap: The module classifies and clusters supplied records but does not yet ingest a broad creator corpus or discover new companies automatically.
gaps.impact_inference: It is high-precision but recall-limited and biased toward companies already selected for research.

gaps.subject: MangoBD current sponsor-cluster module
gaps.fact: MangoBD correctly separates confirmed paid disclosures, affiliate/referral evidence and unverified mentions, and carries evidence_ids into clusters and creator-brand pairs.
gaps.observed_gap: The sponsorship observation contract does not yet store extraction source, raw brand, canonical brand id, mention type, numeric confidence or transcript timestamp as first-class fields.
gaps.impact_inference: Scaling extraction would be difficult to audit and deduplicate without a richer atomic mention layer.

gaps.subject: MangoBD current sponsor-cluster module
gaps.fact: MangoBD summarizes recurrence within a 45-day window and builds creator-brand pairs.
gaps.observed_gap: It does not yet compute sponsor gaps from peer creators, creator gaps from competitor brands, lapsed repeat deals or share-of-voice with minimum-sample gates.
gaps.impact_inference: The existing data is not yet converted into systematic long-tail company discovery and actionable whitespace.

portable_patterns.pattern: Run deterministic disclosure/link extraction first, then use an LLM only for unresolved spans and semantic classification.
portable_patterns.mangobd_adaptation: Keep MangoBD's paid-versus-affiliate classifier as the authoritative first layer. The LLM may propose entities and mention types but cannot promote an observation without a source span and evidence gate.

portable_patterns.source: Separate Sponsorship Intelligence Graph comparator, not Kartr
portable_patterns.pattern: Make one brand mention in one piece of content the atomic record, with raw and canonical brand, source, mention type, timestamp and numeric confidence.
portable_patterns.mangobd_adaptation: Add observation_id, creator_id, project_id or candidate_brand_id, content_id, raw_brand, canonical_brand_id, source_type, disclosure_class, mention_type, matched_excerpt, start_ts, confidence, extractor_version and evidence_id.

portable_patterns.source: Separate Sponsorship Intelligence Graph comparator, not Kartr
portable_patterns.pattern: Build the corpus offline with resumable disk caches, quota accounting and versioned artifacts; serve the graph without request-time extraction.
portable_patterns.mangobd_adaptation: Seed from Solomon-adjacent creators, their creator peers and niche cohorts. Fetch channel uploads through uploads playlists, persist raw metadata once, and rebuild observations and graph deterministically.

portable_patterns.source: Separate Sponsorship Intelligence Graph comparator, not Kartr
portable_patterns.pattern: Require a canonical gazetteer match, tracking signal or repeat observation; maintain aliases, blocklist and creator-owned-domain rules; validate every LLM brand against source text.
portable_patterns.mangobd_adaptation: Use the existing company entity IDs as the canonical registry, add a candidate-brand quarantine table for unknown domains, and require manual review before an unknown company enters priority scoring.

portable_patterns.source: Separate Sponsorship Intelligence Graph comparator, not Kartr
portable_patterns.pattern: Collapse atomic mentions into creator-brand edges while retaining count, firstSeen, lastSeen, all dates, mention types and verifiable evidence links.
portable_patterns.mangobd_adaptation: Keep sponsorship edges separate from X FOLLOWS, MUTUAL_FOLLOW, REPLIES_TO and MENTIONS edges. Overlay them only at query time to produce Solomon to connector to creator to company or operator routes.

portable_patterns.source: Separate Sponsorship Intelligence Graph comparator, not Kartr
portable_patterns.pattern: Find brands sponsoring peer creators but not the focal creator; rank by peer coverage and recency, with explicit peer-set rules.
portable_patterns.mangobd_adaptation: Use Solomon-adjacent AI, crypto and developer creators as roots. Define peers by at least two shared sponsors, then fall back to niche, geography and log audience-size proximity. Send unknown brands into research rather than directly into outreach.

portable_patterns.source: Separate Sponsorship Intelligence Graph comparator, not Kartr
portable_patterns.pattern: For a brand, find creators already bought by category competitors but not by that brand, then rank with an exposed score breakdown.
portable_patterns.mangobd_adaptation: Use this as the value proposition in outreach: show a company the China and APAC creators its nearest competitors activate, plus Mango's verified routing path to those creators.

portable_patterns.source: Separate Sponsorship Intelligence Graph comparator, not Kartr
portable_patterns.pattern: Only calculate momentum, similarity, saturation or lapsed-deal signals when the evidence count clears a declared minimum.
portable_patterns.mangobd_adaptation: Preserve MangoBD's evidence-first policy and add not_enough_history outputs instead of generating weak trend scores from one or two observations.

portable_patterns.source: Kartr response pattern, strengthened for MangoBD
portable_patterns.pattern: Return model_used and raw model response alongside parsed output during development.
portable_patterns.mangobd_adaptation: Persist extractor_version, prompt_version, model, raw output hash and parse status in an audit record; keep raw content out of the production graph but link it through evidence_id.

portable_patterns.source: Separate Sponsorship Intelligence Graph comparator, not Kartr
portable_patterns.pattern: Every creator-brand edge opens the exact supporting videos and transcript timestamp when available.
portable_patterns.mangobd_adaptation: Any broader MangoBD graph should make proof, confidence, relation type and last verified date visible before centrality or path length.

do_not_copy.pattern: Treat a hard-coded list of famous sponsors as the main detector.
do_not_copy.reason: It structurally favors well-known companies and works against the user's goal of finding a wider long tail.

do_not_copy.pattern: Use search.list to enumerate every channel's latest videos.
do_not_copy.reason: It is quota-expensive and unnecessary when the channel uploads playlist can provide the corpus more cheaply and reproducibly.

do_not_copy.pattern: Truncate descriptions before the sponsor extractor runs.
do_not_copy.reason: YouTube sponsor disclosures and tracked links are often below the first 200 characters.

do_not_copy.pattern: Accept LLM high, medium or low confidence without source-span validation or calibration.
do_not_copy.reason: A model label is not evidence and cannot support a confirmed BD relationship edge.

do_not_copy.pattern: Persist sponsors as an untyped list and use only sponsors[0] in the graph.
do_not_copy.reason: It silently loses multi-sponsor videos and makes schema drift undetectable.

do_not_copy.pattern: Use raw display names as graph node IDs.
do_not_copy.reason: Aliases, spelling variants and product names fragment the company graph and corrupt degree metrics.

do_not_copy.pattern: Use an undirected simple graph that collapses repeated observations and drops evidence, dates and relation type.
do_not_copy.reason: It cannot distinguish one mention from a repeat paid relationship or keep X routing separate from commercial history.

do_not_copy.pattern: Let an LLM invent a fit score in a preselected 60-99 range.
do_not_copy.reason: The score is compressed, uncalibrated and not comparable across runs. MangoBD should retain explicit reachability, spend, timing, fit, buyer clarity and evidence components.

do_not_copy.pattern: Add subscriber-count bonuses as a default relevance signal.
do_not_copy.reason: It reintroduces fame bias, while MangoBD intentionally lets a routable mid-market target outrank a famous cold target.

do_not_copy.pattern: Mix broad web-search recommendations with proven sponsorship history in one result type.
do_not_copy.reason: A search result is a lead, not proof of budget, campaign history or relationship.

do_not_copy.pattern: Use graph degree centrality as a proxy for introducibility.
do_not_copy.reason: Popularity in a sponsor graph does not prove a Solomon-rooted X path, human willingness or an operator-level route.
